evidence: No restatement, material weakness or management-integrity issue was identified in the supplied filings.
PwC has audited the company since FY2014, eight of ten director nominees were independent and all board committees were independent.
The company held $8.63B of cash and investments at June 30, 2026 and generated $1.973B of H1 operating cash flow.
There is no meaningful financial-debt burden and current growth is internally funded.
June period-end shares declined from 358.4M to 353.9M year over year as repurchases exceeded equity issuance.
TTM SBC was material but manageable at approximately 7.6% of revenue; the 2026 equity-plan increase adds potential future issuance and should be monitored.
Revenue growth is supported by procedure growth, rising utilization, installed-base expansion and 85% recurring revenue rather than subsidies or promotional acquisition.
H1 2026 operating income grew 38% on 21% revenue growth, while TTM FCF margin was approximately 29.2%.
Inventory and lease asset intensity are rising but do not currently indicate structural incremental-return collapse.
Installed base, procedure volume, utilization and recurring revenue remain positive, and da Vinci 5 is scaling.
Competition is increasing, especially in China, but no persistent consolidated moat contraction is evident.
At a 30% year-ten FCF margin, the reverse DCF requires approximately 14.1% annual revenue growth for ten years.
That requirement is demanding and close to the modeled Base case, but it is not unrealistic relative to current procedure growth and platform opportunities.
Economics are concentrated in the da Vinci ecosystem, but revenue is diversified across procedures, geographies, hospitals, consumables, service and leases.
No fatal single-customer or single-regulation dependence was identified.
Substantial net cash, recurring revenue, broad procedure exposure and positive FCF make bankruptcy or permanent loss from ordinary cyclical stress unlikely.
Product-safety, regulatory and antitrust events remain the most credible permanent-impairment paths but are not currently probable enough to trigger a veto.
